([[Encino, Los Angeles|Encino, California]]) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team1 = [[Westchester Knicks]] | years2 = {{nbay|2021|full=y}} | team2 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years3 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team3 = [[College Park Skyhawks]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = [[Osceola Magic]] | years5 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team5 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years6 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team6 = →[[Texas Legends]] | years7 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team7 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | highlights = }} '''Brandon Tory Williams'''{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2025 |title=Calling NBA Players by their government names |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@dallasmavs/video/7555914947490843917 |access-date=November 6, 2025 |website=[[TikTok]]}} (born November 22, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Williams attended [[Crespi Carmelite High School]] in [[Encino, Los Angeles|Encino, California]], where he was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in May 2018.{{cite news |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Arizona basketball: Brandon Williams moving on from Wildcats |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2020/09/05/arizona-basketball-brandon-williams-moving-wildcats/5728176002/ |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=September 5, 2020}} ==College career== Williams played the 2018–19 season for the Wildcats, averaging 11.4 [[points per game]] and earning honorable mention [[Pac-12 Conference]] All-Freshman team honors. He had knee surgery in 2019, missing what would have been his sophomore season. He left Arizona in 2020 to heal and to prepare for his eventual professional career.{{cite web|last=Pascoe|first=Bruce|title=As NBA Draft nears, ex-Arizona guard Brandon Williams looking elsewhere|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/as-nba-draft-nears-ex-arizona-guard-brandon-williams-looking-elsewhere/article_b29b84ca-ef0d-11eb-81ba-0700f6485ca0.html|website=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=July 28, 2021|access-date=December 27, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers / Westchester Knicks (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Williams joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]] in October 2021.{{cite web |title=Westchester Knicks Announce Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/westchester-knicks-announce-training-camp-roster/n-5758531 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=December 27, 2021 |date=October 26, 2021}} He averaged 17.7 points, 4 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game in 10 games. On December 26, 2021, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) signed Williams to a 10-day contract to fill out the roster after several players were lost due to [[COVID-19]] health and safety protocols.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers sign three players to 10-day contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-three-players-10-day-contracts|website=[[NBA.com]]|date=December 26, 2021|access-date=December 27, 2021}} On January 5, 2022, Williams was re-acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 5, 2022|access-date=January 5, 2022}} On January 22, he scored a career-high 35 points and had eight assists in a 142–117 loss to the [[Maine Celtics]].{{cite web |last1=Priczak |first1=Chris |title=Westchester Knicks trounced by Maine Celtics, 126–99 |url=https://www.postingandtoasting.com/2022/1/24/22897075/westchester-knicks-trounced-by-maine-celtics-126-99 |website=Posting and Toasting |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=January 30, 2022 |date=January 24, 2022}} On February 22, 2022, Williams signed a two-way contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN DREW EUBANKS AND BRANDON WILLIAMS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-drew-eubanks-and-brandon-williams|url-status=live|access-date=February 22, 2022|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222221921/https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-drew-eubanks-and-brandon-williams |archive-date=February 22, 2022}} He was waived on October 7.{{cite web|author=porfgomez|title=Trail Blazers waive Devontae Cacok, Wes Iwundu and Brandon Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-devontae-cacok-wes-iwundu-and-brandon-williams|date=October 7, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2022}} ===College Park Skyhawks (2022–2023)=== On November 4, 2022, Williams was named to the opening night roster for the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/roster|website=gleague.nba.com|title=College Park Skyhawks Roster 2022–23|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===Osceola Magic (2023)=== On September 12, 2023, Williams signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agents Trevelin Queen and Brandon Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agents-trevelin-queen-brandon-williams-20230912|website=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2023|access-date=September 13, 2023}} but was waived on October 21.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Waive Mac McClung, Daeqwon Plowden and Brandon Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-waive-mac-mcclung-daeqwon-plowden-brandon-williams-20231021|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 28, 2023}} On November 2, he joined the [[Osceola Magic]].{{cite web|title=Training Camp Roster Just Dropped|url=https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-just-dropped|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2023–2026)=== On December 28, 2023, Williams signed a two-way contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|title=Mavs sign Brandon Williams to two-way contract, waive Dexter Dennis|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-brandon-williams-to-two-way-contract-waive-dexter-dennis|website=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023}} Williams reached the [[2024 NBA Finals]] where the Mavericks lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|website=CBSNews.com|date=June 17, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2024}} He was re-signed on July 12, 2024, to a two-way contract.{{cite web|title=Mavericks re-sign Brandon Williams to two-way contract|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/mavericks-re-sign-brandon-williams-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2024|access-date=July 12, 2024}} On March 7, 2025, Williams recorded a career-high 31 points against the [[2024–25 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web|title=Mavericks guard scores career-high in loss to Memphis Grizzlies|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavericks-guard-scores-career-high-in-loss-to-memphis-grizzlies-brandon-williams|access-date=March 12, 2025|website=si.com}} On April 8, he was signed to a multi-year contract by the Mavericks.{{Cite web|title=Mavericks Sign Brandon Williams|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-brandon-williams|access-date=April 10, 2025|website=nba.com}} Williams made 33 appearances (including three starts) for Dallas during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 8.3 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Brandon Williams 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397040/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=June 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Williams played in 66 games (starting 16) for the Mavericks during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 13.0 points (a career-high), 2.9 rebounds, and 3.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=Brandon Williams 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397040/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=June 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Golden State Warriors (2026–present) === On August 26, 2026, Williams signed a one-year contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Guard Brandon Williams |url= https://warriors.com/news/warriors-sign-free-agent-guard-brandon-williams-20260826 |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=warriors.com |language=en}} ==Personal life== On October 25, 2025, Williams was arrested at [[Dallas Fort Worth International Airport]] after less than 2 ounces of marijuana were found in his luggage.{{Cite web |date=October 30, 2025 |title=Mavs' Williams sorry for arrest, being 'distraction' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46775728/mavericks-brandon-williams-apologizes-being-distraction-following-arrest |access-date=December 5, 2025
